answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a horizon as the anchor of the cost. A terrace stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a nectar...
